kuzushi.summary: Draw uke forward or forward-diagonal while lowering under the center of gravity.

tsukuri.summary: Enter under uke with shoulder and hip alignment appropriate to the variant.

kake.summary: Rotate and project uke over the shoulder line.

mechanicsTheme: Shoulder-wheel family: tori lowers under uke's center, loads uke across the shoulder line, and rotates them forward or forward-diagonally. The exact grip, entry, and off-balancing line depend heavily on the variant.

kuzushi.summary: Load uke backward or back-diagonal as their attack commits forward.

tsukuri.summary: Fit behind or under uke's center while maintaining control of the upper body.

kake.summary: Sacrifice backward and project uke over the rear line under control.

kuzushi.summary: Draw uke forward while lowering into a rear sacrifice position.

tsukuri.summary: Place the lifting foot while sitting under uke's center with sleeve and lapel control.

kake.summary: Extend and rotate uke forward over the body line.

kuzushi.summary: Draw uke forward or forward-diagonal into a corner of balance.

tsukuri.summary: Enter beneath uke with a rear sacrifice position and lifting leg placement.

kake.summary: Lift and rotate uke over the diagonal corner line.

kuzushi.summary: Pull uke forward and down into a committed reaction.

tsukuri.summary: Drop under uke while maintaining pulling control, often from over-the-back or belt control.

kake.summary: Continue the pull and roll uke through the sacrifice action.

kuzushi.summary: Use uke's forward pressure, commonly from a low attack or bent posture.

tsukuri.summary: Wrap and load uke while dropping into rear sacrifice position.

kake.summary: Roll backward and lift to reverse uke over the body line.

mechanicsTheme: Kata sequence note: uki-goshi is a turn-entry hip throw, but Nage-no-kata demonstrates the left-hand version first as an exception. For ordinary lookup, model side by tori side first, then derive the absolute rotation from that side.

Turn-entry hip throw: model as a standard-side hip turn for the selected tori side. Absolute clockwise or counter-clockwise rotation should be derived from right/left tori side rather than treated as the variant name.
Rotational hip-wheel entry: model side by tori's chosen hip side first. Absolute clockwise or counter-clockwise turn should be displayed as a derived detail.
Lifting-pulling hip entry: model as a standard-side fit-in for the selected tori side. The rotation label should mirror when the tori-side switch changes.
Sweeping hip entry: model side by tori's sweeping hip/leg side first. The rotation direction is derived from tori side, not a separate left/right-turn variant.
Belt-grip hip throw: model as a standard-side hip entry for the selected tori side. The belt grip changes control, but the left/right display should still mirror from tori side.
Spring hip entry: model side by tori's springing hip/leg side first. Absolute rotation should be derived from tori side and not used as the primary variant label.
Sleeve-controlled turn entry: model as standard-side or drop-entry relative to the selected tori side. This avoids treating clockwise/counter-clockwise as the main variant identity.

One-arm seoi uses a standard-side turn for ordinary right/left tori entries. Reverse or Korean-style entries should be modeled as reverse-turn variants; absolute clockwise/counter-clockwise is derived from the selected tori side.
Shoulder-drop entries inherit the seoi side model: standard-side or reverse-turn relative to tori side, with drop mechanics as the entry modifier.
Body-drop turn entry: model as a standard-side fit-in for the selected tori side. Absolute clockwise/counter-clockwise should be derived for display rather than treated as a named variant.

aliases: arm triangle hold from side control

mechanicsTheme: Outer reap side model: the tori-side toggle should describe the reaping leg and outside line. This is not a reverse-turn variant; right and left versions mirror the attacking leg, support step, and backward-diagonal pressure.

Counter to o-soto-gari: model the side by the incoming reap and tori's returning reap line. The important chirality is which leg is being attacked and which leg returns the counter, not clockwise/counter-clockwise turn.
Inner reap side model: the tori-side toggle should describe the reaping leg and inside line. Right/left versions mirror the attacking leg, driving shoulder line, and uke's backward-diagonal balance.

Minor inner reap side model: the tori-side toggle should describe the small inside attacking foot and uke's near-foot line. Ko-uchi counters can be evasion-based or pressure-based, but the side label is still leg/foot line rather than turn direction.

Shoulder-throw family: model standard-side seoi and reverse-turn seoi separately. For right tori, standard-side seoi rotates counter-clockwise and reverse-turn seoi rotates clockwise; left tori mirrors those rotations.

names.kana: けさがためののがれかた

kuzushi.summary: Build a frame against uke's hip or shoulder line and prevent the head-and-arm hold from fully flattening the torso.

tsukuri.summary: Turn toward uke, recover the trapped arm line when possible, and make enough hip space to face the hold.

kake.summary: Come to the knees, recover guard, or reverse before uke resets scarf-hold pressure.

names.kana: よこしほうがためののがれかた

kuzushi.summary: Create a defensive frame to interrupt chest pressure and redirect top control away from the center line.

tsukuri.summary: Turn onto the side, make hip space, and insert knee or shin as a wedge.

kake.summary: Recover guard, come to knees, or recompose to a safer defensive position.

names.kana: よこしほうがためののがれかた

kuzushi.summary: Use an underhook, far-hip, or belt connection to prevent the top player from flattening the shoulders.

tsukuri.summary: Turn toward uke, bring the near elbow inside, and connect the hips under the top pressure.

kake.summary: Come to knees, reverse, or recover guard using the hip-control connection.

names.kana: たてしほうがためののがれかた

kuzushi.summary: Trap one side of uke and load their weight onto the blocked post.

tsukuri.summary: Bridge through the hips while keeping uke from posting with the trapped arm or leg.

kake.summary: Roll over the trapped side and transition to top or guard-safe posture.

names.kana: たてしほうがためののがれかた

kuzushi.summary: Frame against uke and shift their weight enough to make knee space.

tsukuri.summary: Connect elbow to knee, turn onto the side, and slide one knee inside the mount line.

kake.summary: Recover half guard or full guard while maintaining frames against renewed pressure.

names.kana: かみしほうがためののがれかた

kuzushi.summary: Frame against uke to keep the shoulders from being pinned flat and turn the head-side pressure off the center line.

tsukuri.summary: Bring the elbows inside, turn toward a side, and make enough hip angle to avoid being followed head-to-head.

kake.summary: Recover guard, turn to knees, or recompose to a side-control-safe frame before uke settles the hold again.

mechanicsTheme: Timing foot-sweep side model: the tori-side toggle should describe the sweeping foot and uke's advancing foot. The key distinction is timing and foot line, not a turn variant.
Counter to de-ashi-harai: model side by the foot that evades the sweep and the foot that immediately returns the sweep. This is an evasion-and-return timing problem, not a reverse-turn entry.
Counter to o-uchi-gari: model side by the incoming inside reap and tori's returning reap or lift line. The side changes the legs and pressure line rather than creating a separate turn variant.
Inner-thigh throw side model: the tori-side toggle should describe the lifting/sweeping leg and hip line. Right and left versions mirror the attacking leg and forward-diagonal projection.
Counter to uchi-mata: model side by the incoming inner-thigh attack and the returning counter line. The relevant chirality is leg/hip line and balance recovery, not absolute rotation.

kuzushi.summary: Draw uke forward or forward-diagonal while controlling the lapel-side upper body connection.

tsukuri.summary: Turn under the controlled lapel and arm line while avoiding a trapped-arm or shoulder-locking finish.

kake.summary: Project uke forward over the shoulder line with enough release and rotation to avoid arm entanglement.

mechanicsTheme: Lapel-based shoulder-throw family often described in English as reverse or Korean seoi-nage. It is modeled as its own searchable technique because the grip, turn, and arm-entanglement risk differ enough from standard seoi-nage to matter in lookup and safety views. Treat it as a reverse-turn seoi family entry: right tori rotates clockwise, left tori rotates counter-clockwise.

Propping foot side model: the tori-side toggle should describe the blocking/propping foot and lifting-pulling line. The throw works through foot placement and diagonal draw rather than a named left/right-turn variant.
Knee-wheel side model: the tori-side toggle should describe the propping leg and wheel line. The important side detail is which knee/leg line is blocked while uke is rotated over it.
Minor outer reap side model: the tori-side toggle should describe the outside attacking foot and uke's near-foot line. This mirrors by attacking leg and balance line rather than by turn direction.
Sliding foot-sweep side model: the tori-side toggle should describe the sweeping foot and the direction both of uke's feet are carried. Timing, spacing, and foot line matter more than turn chirality.
Minor outer hook side model: the tori-side toggle should describe the hooking leg and outside control line. Right/left versions mirror the hook and backward-diagonal pressure.
Leg-wheel side model: the tori-side toggle should describe the blocking leg and wheel line. The side cue is leg placement across uke's path, with rotation derived from the selected side.
Major lifting hip throw: model as a belt-grip hip entry on the selected tori side. The absolute rotation should be derived from the right/left tori-side toggle.
Minor lifting hip throw: model as a belt-grip hip entry on the selected tori side. The absolute rotation should be derived from the right/left tori-side toggle.

Sweeping lifting-pulling foot side model: the tori-side toggle should describe the sweeping foot and tsurikomi line. The throw mirrors through foot placement and lifting-pulling pressure, not a reverse-turn variant.

はだかじめのふせぎかた

kuzushi.summary: Create space, posture, or hand position that interrupts hadaka-jime's control before the finish is settled.

tsukuri.summary: Protect the vulnerable line, clear the controlling limb or grip, and angle toward a safer defensive frame.

kake.summary: Recover guard, turn out, stack safely, or return to a neutral ne-waza position depending on the attack.
